hypothesis: If Darwin is right, then among oceanic islands (volcanic or otherwise never connected to a continent) a substantial fraction have more than half of their native species endemic, and their endemic proportion is clearly higher than that of area-matched mainland or continental-shelf regions.
pass_criterion: Using native vascular plant checklists with at least 20 native species, BOTH conditions hold. (a) At least 20% of oceanic islands have an endemic proportion (endemic native species / native species) of at least 0.30, and at least 10% have 0.50 or more. (b) Within log10-area bins (one bin per order of magnitude), the median endemic proportion of oceanic islands exceeds that of continental islands and mainland regions by at least 0.10 in a majority of bins that hold at least 10 units of each type. A one-sided Mann-Whitney test, pooled by bin, must give p < 0.01.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if either condition fails. Condition (a) fails if fewer than 10% of oceanic islands reach an endemic proportion of 0.30, or fewer than 5% reach 0.50. Condition (b) fails if the area-matched median difference is below 0.05 in most bins, or if the pooled test gives p >= 0.05. Some oceanic islands will have zero endemics, so the claim is about prevalence ("often") and not about every island.
interpretation: Darwin's "oceanic islands" map to islands flagged as oceanic or volcanic in the island geology field, as opposed to continental fragment or shelf islands. "Kinds of inhabitants" and "species" map to native vascular plant species counts, the best-sampled group on islands. This is a modern taxonomic reinterpretation, since Darwin also cited birds, land snails and insects. "Endemic" maps to species recorded as restricted to the checklist entity, or in modern usage to the single island or archipelago. Endemic proportion is endemic species divided by native species, and the "relative to area" part is tested by comparing against area-matched non-oceanic units. Darwin's causal clause (colonists being especially liable to modification) is not tested here, only the empirical generalisation. Caveat: the exact GIFT field names for endemism and geology were not visible on the pages I fetched. They need checking in the API documentation before analysis begins.

dataset.name: GIFT (Global Inventory of Floras and Traits)
dataset.publisher: Biodiversity, Macroecology and Biogeography group, University of Göttingen
dataset.why_it_fits: GIFT is a database of regional and island plant checklists. It is accessible through an API and the CRAN GIFT R package (10.32614/CRAN.package.GIFT). It is meant to supply native and endemic species counts per checklist, together with environmental data for each region (area, island status and geology). That gives the endemic proportion for each island, split by oceanic and non-oceanic type and by area. I could not confirm the endemism and geology fields from the pages I fetched, because the GIFT website loads dynamically and the CRAN page does not list them. The plan assumes they exist and says so.
